conclusion.scope: GitHub issue #70 bounded Android runtime-permission reliability fault-injection slice; no security-business, security-certification, goldset, or benchmark-metric claim
conclusion.rationale: The canonical accountable pair is internally consistent and independently reproducible from its durable evidence: the baseline demonstrates first denial, permanent denial, grant, and post-revocation graceful degradation, while the matched candidate exposes both a denial dead end and an uncaught AndroidRuntime SecurityException after revocation. Package-manager postconditions, UI layouts/screenshots, Journey command output, logcat, APK installation hashes, host revisions, device identity, and oracle verdicts agree without contradiction.

gaps: The slice covers one debug-only Wikipedia fixture on one API 35 emulator, not a device/API compatibility matrix.

External revocation is modeled deterministically with a device-scoped package-manager event; the run does not navigate through the Settings UI to revoke permission, although the baseline visibly exposes the Settings route after permanent denial.
Android CLI cannot device-select screen capture with two online devices, so device-scoped adb supplies raw screenshots and capture manifests explicitly record annotated screenshots as unavailable.
Candidate L3 is intentionally gated after deterministic L1/L2 failures; no candidate L3 claim is made.

At audit time this conclusion and the final run-level checksums manifest still require generation/commit by the owning implementation agent before GitHub issue closure; the substantive evidence is sufficient, but it must not be represented as committed durable GitHub evidence until that occurs.
